gaps.sentence: The hotel was fully booked. ___, we found a room at a guesthouse nearby.
gaps.explanation: Finding a room contradicts the expected failure: However signals the contrast.

gaps.sentence: She speaks fluent Mandarin; ___, she reads classical Chinese.
gaps.explanation: 'Moreover' adds a further, even more remarkable achievement.

gaps.sentence: Cut the onions, fry them gently and ___, stir in the cream.
gaps.hint: the last step of a sequence
gaps.explanation: 'Finally' closes a list of actions; 'firstly' opens one, while 'initially'/'at first' contrast with later events.

gaps.sentence: I will send the report today ___ you asked for it early.
Hardly had we arrived ___ the storm broke.
gaps.explanation: 'Hardly... when' is the fixed pair for one event interrupting another.

gaps.sentence: I can't afford a holiday this year; ___, I can't get the time off work.
gaps.explanation: 'Besides' adds a further, often decisive, reason in informal style.

gaps.sentence: The flight was delayed ___ thick fog.
gaps.explanation: 'Because of' + noun phrase gives the cause; although/despite express contrast.

gaps.sentence: ___ the strike, trains will run a reduced service all week.
gaps.explanation: 'Because of the strike' gives the reason for the reduced service.
